primary.name: Official Astro minimal starter
primary.licenseObligations: Preserve the Astro MIT copyright and license notice in third-party notices.
primary.modificationSummary: Retain the already-approved and implemented Astro application shell without replacement.
primary.contributionBoundary: The sole application framework, file router, content-collection foundation, and static build model.

secondary.name: AstroPaper
secondary.licenseObligations: No source is copied. Preserve this record as provenance for the conceptual reference.
secondary.modificationSummary: Reference its complete theme-token coverage, restrained responsive shell, accessible navigation behavior, and compact spacing cadence without copying source or adopting dependencies.
secondary.contributionBoundary: Conceptual reference for full-site dark and light theming, laptop-width rhythm, and mobile header behavior only.

requiredApprovals: Retain the previously approved official Astro minimal scaffold and exact package architecture.
Use AstroPaper only as a conceptual visual-system reference with no copied source and no added dependency.
conflicts: No Tailwind foundation, blog, MDX content, search, RSS, React runtime, second router, second content system, analytics, or deployment model will be introduced.
No external repository may replace the existing Astro application shell or factual content model.
No decorative artwork or background imagery will be reintroduced.
remainingUncertainty: Turkish copy still requires user review.
Headshot and optional project media remain deferred.
Physical-device review remains necessary after deployment.

rejectedFinalists.reason: Rejected by the evaluation hard gate despite its stars and strong single-page fit: it has no release, CI, or tests, its mobile navigation is hidden, it has no dark theme, and adopting its Astro 5 and Tailwind foundations would conflict with the approved architecture.
Rejected because its large Next.js, React, Tailwind, motion, and component-registry architecture is disproportionate to this static single-page portfolio and conflicts with the approved foundations.
Rejected for the website refinement because it is a compact CV page rather than a project-led portfolio; it remains covered by the earlier print-only conceptual boundary.
